report.title: Rich feature completion reports
report.scope_note: Example feature-route report for the delivery-report skill itself.
report.constraints: The report presents evidence; git, tests, reviewer gates, and deployment receipts establish completion. Never mark owner-held validation as passed.

executive_summary: Completed features can now ship with a durable visual report that explains the delivered behavior, practical value, validation evidence, and residual limitations in plain English. The report source remains structured and auditable, while the generated HTML is portable, self-contained, and theme-aware. This example is verified against the bundled renderer and tests.
problem: Feature closeouts were split across plans, diffs, test logs, and agent summaries, making it expensive for a stakeholder to understand what changed and why it matters.
solution: The delivery-report skill introduces one evidence-linked manifest and a deterministic renderer that combines narrative, findings, validation, screenshots or illustrations, and small native graphics into one offline HTML artifact.

value_adds.title: Faster stakeholder comprehension
value_adds.detail: Readers get the outcome and value before implementation detail, without reconstructing the feature from engineering artifacts.

value_adds.title: Truthful, portable evidence
value_adds.detail: The HTML embeds local media and preserves exact validation and residual-state labels while remaining usable offline in both light and dark themes.

changes.plain_english: Large completed features now have a standard rich report at closeout.
changes.technical_detail: Tier eligibility and the report path are integrated into the dev-execution completion contract.

changes.plain_english: Screenshots, illustrations, metrics, and architecture flows travel inside one HTML file.
changes.technical_detail: Media is encoded as data URIs and declarative graphics are rendered as inline SVG; a four-block token system makes both themes first-class.

key_points: The source manifest is canonical; HTML is derived.
Rendering never calls a model or the network.
A rendered report does not replace tests, reviewer approval, or deployment receipts.

findings.title: Visual evidence needs an explicit truth boundary
findings.detail: Generated illustrations can explain architecture but must not be presented as product screenshots.
findings.impact: The manifest separates screenshot and illustration media types, requires captions, and records the generating provider.

validation.name: Unit and cross-project smoke tests
validation.result: Renderer, eligibility, validation, media embedding, and safety checks passed.

timeline.label: Evidence locked
timeline.detail: Completion truth and exact validation results were collected.

timeline.label: Report authored
timeline.detail: Plain-English value, changes, findings, and visuals were linked to evidence.

timeline.label: Artifact validated
timeline.detail: The self-contained HTML passed safety and integrity checks.

diagrams.title: Completion-report flow
diagrams.caption: Canonical evidence becomes a structured report manifest and then a portable presentation artifact.

no_visual_reason: This example ships without embedded media so the repository stays lightweight; the diagram above carries the visual explanation.
risks: Reports can become stale if edited after the exact-tree review without revalidation.
Sensitive screenshots must be redacted before embedding.

followups.title: Wire Artifact Atlas catalog ingestion
followups.detail: Attach the generated HTML + manifest to the catalog once the hosting contract ships.

handoff.prompt: Scope catalog ingestion for delivery-report artifacts: attach the rendered HTML and its canonical manifest through the Artifact Atlas hosting contract when it lands. Keep render offline; ingestion is a separate approved action.
